clone.title: Clone server
clone.description: Create a copy of this server on the same node to try changes without touching the original.
clone.copyFilesOn: Every file is copied: worlds, plugins and configuration. A large world can take a few minutes.
clone.copyFilesOff: The copy starts empty, with the same template. You will need to install it from Administration.

notCopied.address: Address and port (a new one is assigned)

clone.runningHint: If you copy it now, the world may be caught mid-save. Stop it first for a clean copy.
clone.installingHint: The server is installing. Wait until it finishes to copy all of its files.
clone.stopHint: For a clean copy of the world, stop the server before cloning it.
clone.sameNode: The copy is created on the same node as the original.
clone.confirmWithFiles: “{{name}}” will be created with the settings, users and all the files of “{{source}}”. The original does not change.
clone.confirmWithoutFiles: “{{name}}” will be created with the settings and users of “{{source}}”, without files. The original does not change.
clone.confirmRunning: The server is running: the world may be copied mid-save.
clone.doneCopying: The files are being copied in the background. Follow the progress on the copy's console; you can start it as soon as it finishes.
clone.doneEmpty: The copy is empty. Open it and install it from Administration to get started.

map.title: World map
map.description: Install a web map in one click and explore your world from the panel, with players live.

bluemap.description: Explore the world in 3D as if flying over it. The first render takes a while and uses CPU meanwhile.

dynmap.description: The familiar flat map, light and well known. Less striking, but fine on modest servers.

map.eula: I agree to BlueMap downloading Minecraft's resources (Mojang's EULA)
map.eulaHint: BlueMap needs the game's textures to draw the map and downloads them from Mojang's servers.
map.restartNote: The server is on: it will restart to load the map.
map.offNote: The map starts the next time you turn the server on.
map.restoreNote: A restore point is saved first, in case you want to go back.
map.failedTitle: The map could not be installed
map.started: {{name}} is being installed. You can follow the steps in the console.
map.installingHint: It is downloaded from Modrinth and, if the server is on, the server restarts to load it. You can follow each step in the console.
map.offTitle: Turn the server on to see the map
map.offHint: {{name}} is installed and starts with the server.
map.starting: The map shows up here as soon as it is ready.
map.startError: The server could not be started.

preparingHint.bluemap: BlueMap is being configured and is downloading the game's resources. The first time can take a couple of minutes; this page updates by itself.
preparingHint.dynmap: Dynmap is starting its web server. It can take a minute; this page updates by itself.

map.removeDescription: The map's plugin or mod is deleted. What is already drawn stays in the files, in case you install it again. The change applies the next time you restart the server.
map.removed: Restart the server so it stops loading.
map.removeError: The map could not be removed.
map.loadErrorTitle: The map could not be loaded

map.unsupportedTitle: The map needs Paper, Fabric or Forge
map.unsupportedVanilla: This server runs vanilla Minecraft, which loads no plugins or mods. Switch the loader to Paper, Fabric, Forge or NeoForge to install the map.
map.unsupportedUnknown: We cannot tell which loader this server uses. The map works with Paper, Fabric, Forge and NeoForge.

modpacks.title: Modpacks
modpacks.description: Install a whole modpack from Modrinth or CurseForge in one click. The panel sets up the loader, the Minecraft version and the Java version it needs.
modpacks.statusError: Could not load the modpack status.

installed.versionLocked: The modpack sets the Minecraft version; to change it, install another version of the pack.

intro.title: No modpack installed
intro.description: Pick a modpack from the list. A restore point is saved before it is installed, so you can always go back.

source.label: Modpack source
source.curseforgeMissing: CurseForge needs an API key that the administrator has not set up yet.
source.curseforgeMissingAdmin: To use CurseForge, add the API key in the panel settings.

search.label: Search modpacks
search.placeholder: Search a modpack, e.g. All the Mods
search.emptyDescription: Try other words or search the other source.
search.errorDescription: Modrinth or CurseForge did not answer. Try again in a moment.

dialog.title: Install {{title}}
dialog.description: Pick the version of the modpack. The panel takes care of the rest.
dialog.noVersions: This modpack has no versions the panel can install (Fabric, Forge or NeoForge with a server pack).
dialog.freshWorldHint: Deletes the current world and generates a new one with the modpack. Off, your world is kept.

steps.stop: The server stops if it is running.
steps.restorePoint: A restore point is saved in Backups.
steps.replace: Mods, configuration and the loader are replaced with the modpack's.
steps.world: Your world, server.properties and the player lists are kept.
steps.worldFresh: The current world is deleted and a new one is created; server.properties and the player lists are kept.
steps.start: Java {{java}} with {{loader}} for Minecraft {{version}} is used, and the server starts again if it was running.
steps.startUnknown: Java and the Minecraft version are set, and the server starts again if it was running.

dialog.memoryHint: This server has {{memory}} MB of memory. Most modpacks need at least 4096 MB and may not start with less.

progress.title: Installing {{title}}
progress.hint: You can follow every step in the console. Do not start the server until it finishes.

steps.cleaning: Removing the previous mods and configuration…
steps.loader: Installing the loader (this can take a few minutes)…
steps.curseforge: Downloading and installing the CurseForge server pack…

result.doneHint: The first start of a modpack takes longer than usual while it generates its files.
result.failed: The modpack could not be installed.

toast.started: {{title}} is being installed. Follow the progress here or in the console.

modpacks.safety: A restore point is saved in Backups before the install. If the modpack gives trouble, restore it and you are back where you were.

nodes.title: Node Management
nodes.description: Manage all deployment nodes for your servers.

addDialog.title: Create Node
addDialog.useDifferentHostLabel: Use a different host/port for server-to-server communication
addDialog.useDifferentHostDescription: This separate address is used when the main node needs to communicate with the new node. This is useful, for example, when the nodes are on the same network behind NAT.
addDialog.description: Register a machine that will run servers. You can deploy the daemon on it afterwards.

editDialog.title: Edit Node
editDialog.description: Change the node's name and connection addresses.

deployDialog.title: Deploy Node: {{name}}
deployDialog.description: This node will be used as a slave: it adds capacity to run servers on another machine while the master panel centralizes management. The server will only run the Daemon (SKYPANEL_PANEL_ENABLE=false) and connect to this Panel.
deployDialog.step1: Step 1: Install Docker on the new server.
deployDialog.step1Description: Install Docker Engine and the Docker Compose plugin on the machine that will become the slave node. Since AetherPanel runs in Docker, you do not need to configure an additional Panel, only the Daemon.
deployDialog.step2Description: Create the folder where you will place the docker-compose.yml file and the SkyPanel data folders:
deployDialog.step3Description: Create a docker-compose.yml file in that folder with the following content. With SKYPANEL_PANEL_ENABLE=false the local Panel is disabled and the Daemon points to the master (adjust the master IP if it differs from this URL):
deployDialog.step4Description: Run the following command so the Daemon starts inside Docker and securely connects to the Master Panel:
deployDialog.successMessage: Your new slave node is configured and connected. You can now assign servers to it from the Master Panel!

databaseHosts.title: Database Hosts

addDialog.title: Add New Database Host
addDialog.description: Follow the steps to connect a new database host.

step1.alertDescription1: Currently, only MySQL/MariaDB databases are supported for database hosts.
step1.alertDescription2: Is the panel and database not on the same server? Make sure to allow external access.
step1.userDescription: The username of an account that has sufficient permissions to create new users and databases on the system.
step1.passwordDescription: The password for the database user. It must match the password used in the SQL commands from Step 2.

step2.userDescription: Use mysql -u root -p to access the mysql CLI.
step2.passwordNote: Replace your_strong_password with a real password and type the same value in the Password field (Step 1). If the panel runs inside Docker, it connects from its own container IP, so the user must be created for '%' (any host) as shown above.
step2.exitMysql: To exit the mysql CLI run exit.
step2.externalAccessDescription1: You will likely need to allow external access to this MySQL instance. Locate your my.cnf file (you can use find /etc -iname my.cnf).
step2.externalAccessDescription2: Open my.cnf, add the text below to the end of the file and save it:
step2.externalAccessDescription3: Restart MySQL/MariaDB to apply the changes. Make sure to allow the MySQL port (default 3306) in your firewall.

step3.hostNameDescription: A unique name to identify this host on the panel.
step3.connectionHostDescription: The IP address or domain name that should be used when trying to connect to this MySQL host from this Panel.
step3.portDescription: The port that MySQL is running on for this host.
step3.dbLimitDescription: Maximum number of databases. Leave blank or 0 for unlimited.
step3.linkedNodesDescription: This setting only sets this database host as the default.

databaseHosts.notAuthorized: You don't have permission to view this page.

settings.title: Panel Settings
settings.description: Manage the global settings for your Aether Panel instance.

general.title: General Settings
general.baseUrlDescription: The link from which you will access the control panel following the format: http://localhost:8080
general.companyNameDescription: The name of your organization displayed across the panel interface.
general.masterNodeIpDescription: If multiple panels share a database, set the true Master IP here (e.g. panel.example.com). ALL panels will sync this and route LocalNode transfers properly.
general.geminiApiKeyDescription: Enter your Google Gemini API key to enable artificial intelligence features.
general.hideAiAnalysisDescription: If enabled, the AI console analysis feature will be hidden for all servers.
general.headerDecorationsDescription: Shows the decorative animations (gif and video) at the bottom of the sidebar header.
general.allowRegistrationDescription: Self-registered users cannot perform any actions until permissions are granted. Disabling this only prevents direct registration, server invitations and the Users page are not affected.
general.turnstileEnabledDescription: Enables the Cloudflare Turnstile widget on login and registration to block bots. Disabled by default.
general.turnstileSiteKeyDescription: The public site key of your Cloudflare Turnstile widget.
general.turnstileSecretKeyDescription: The secret key used by the server to verify tokens. Never share it.

sections.panelDescription: Your organization's name and the addresses the panel is reached at.
sections.appearanceDescription: Visual details of the interface for every user.
sections.accessDescription: Who can create an account and how sign-in and sign-up are protected.
sections.modpacksDescription: Key to search and install CurseForge modpacks. Modrinth does not need one.

general.curseforgeKeyDescription: Create it at console.curseforge.com. The main node uses it; remote nodes read the one in their own configuration (daemon.curseforge.key).

updates.title: System updates
updates.description: Update the panel and every registered node to the latest version.
updates.note: The update pulls the latest code from the repository, rebuilds the panel image and restarts the services, including on every registered node. The panel may be unreachable for a few minutes during the process.

status.restartingDescription: Waiting for the panel to come back online. This can take a minute while containers rebuild.
status.updatingDescription: Pulling the latest code and rebuilding images. This usually takes a few minutes.
status.checkFailedDescription: The panel could not reach GitHub to look for new versions.
status.unknownCurrent: Unable to verify the current version
status.unknownCurrentDescription: The deployed commit could not be determined. You can still update manually.
status.availableDescription: A new version of the panel is available.

confirm.title: Update the panel and all nodes?
confirm.description: The latest version will be pulled, images rebuilt and services restarted on every node. The panel and servers may be unreachable for a few minutes.

toast.unreachable: Some nodes could not be reached. Check the node list.
toast.nodesFailed: One or more nodes failed to update. Check the node list.
toast.complete: The panel and all nodes have been updated successfully.
toast.incomplete: Could not trigger the update on: {{nodes}}.
toast.failed: There was a problem starting the update.

offsite.title: Off-site backups
offsite.description: Keep a copy of every backup in S3-compatible storage. If the node's disk fails, the backups are still safe.
offsite.testOk: Connected: a file was written to and deleted from the bucket.
offsite.testError: Could not connect to the storage.
offsite.statusDescription: Local backups are kept; the bucket is a second copy.
offsite.enabledDescription: Each finished backup is uploaded right away. Deleting it removes it from both places.
offsite.onHint: On: new backups will be uploaded to the bucket.
offsite.offHint: Off: backups are only kept on the node.
offsite.bucketDescription: Works with AWS S3, Backblaze B2, Cloudflare R2, Wasabi, MinIO and any S3-compatible service.
offsite.endpointHint: The provider's S3 server, without the bucket name. You can include https://.
offsite.regionHint: Some providers need it; on R2 use "auto".
offsite.keysDescription: A key allowed to read, write and delete in that bucket.
offsite.insecureDescription: Only for a MinIO on your own network. Public providers use https.

domains.title: Automatic subdomains
domains.description: With Cloudflare, every server can have its own address (survival.play.example.com) instead of an IP and port.
domains.testOk: Connection OK: the token can edit the zone {{zone}}.
domains.testError: Could not check the connection to Cloudflare
domains.statusDescription: Owners can pick the name from their server's settings.
domains.autoAssign: Give every new server a subdomain
domains.autoAssignDescription: Derived from the server name (My Survival → my-survival); -2, -3… is added when it is taken.
domains.offHint: Fill in the domain, the token and the zone ID to turn subdomains on.
domains.domainDescription: Where server names are created and what they point to.
domains.baseDomainHint: A domain or subdomain of your Cloudflare zone, for example play.example.com.
domains.baseDomainInvalid: Type just the domain, without http:// or slashes.
domains.targetHint: IP or hostname to point at when a node is registered by hostname or a private address. Empty: each node's public IP.
domains.dnsOnlyNote: Records are created as DNS only (grey cloud), never proxied: game traffic is not HTTP. If the panel's domain goes through Cloudflare's proxy, put the server's public IP here.
domains.credentialsDescription: A token allowed only to edit this zone's DNS. The panel never shows it in its logs.
domains.step1: In Cloudflare, go to My Profile → API Tokens → Create Token and use the "Edit zone DNS" template (Zone → DNS → Edit).
domains.step2: Under "Zone Resources", limit the token to your domain's zone and create it. Copy it: it is shown only once.
domains.step3: The zone ID is on the domain's Overview page, in the right-hand column under API.
domains.zoneIdInvalid: The zone ID has 32 hexadecimal characters (0-9, a-f).
